statement: For the simple undirected unit-transfer graph on all integer partitions of n defined in source.md and problem.md, with d the degree and delta the largest clique containing a vertex minus one: for every integer n>=2, D_delta(n) is 0 for n=2,3, is 1 for 4<=n<=10 and n=12,13, and is 2 for n=11 and all n>=14. For every integer n>=10, put T_s=s(s+1)/2 and choose the unique s with T_s<=n<T_(s+1). Then 4s-8<=D_d(n)<=4s+2, and consequently D_d(n)=4sqrt(2n)+O(1) with an absolute error bound as n tends to infinity. Lower witnesses exist for every n in the claimed ranges. Also orient any edge lambda->mu toward nondecreasing support and let k=r(mu)-r(lambda). Define H(v) to mean that some positive size x>=2 occurs at least twice in v while x-1 is absent. The edge has absolute dimension jump two if and only if either k=1, lambda is neither a staircase nor H and mu is H, or k=2 and both endpoints are H. The separate qualitative localization question in source Problem 8.2 is not asserted resolved; no exact formula for D_d beyond these bounds is asserted.
contribution: One coherent quantitative result: a sharp dimension-jump bound with its complete attainment set and local equality-edge characterization, together with the explicit leading coefficient of degree-jump growth and witnesses for every sufficiently large n. It builds on attributed vertex formulas and support bounds. The three-case dimension reformulation and coarse bound four are not claimed new. No equivalent sharp statement was found in the bounded primary-source screen; priority and mathematical value require fresh review.
